_doc: Lãng Đào Môn lineage (rules-proposals R5). Seat fits Water, Wood (unchanged). Outer gate: ferry-pole-primer (Yellow, Water or Wood). Inner gate and above: washing-waves-canon (Earth, Water first, Wood). Secret arts: returning-wake-verse (existing, learned from the pines' River Hall; inner gate), nine-bends-art (elders and the head). Proposals are unpriced.

secret.note: existing (catalogue-water); taught to the ferrymen by Tùng Đào's River Hall

lineage.tree_route_note: Grand Canal and Spirit Canal: Water that goes round and arrives cheap, the ferry master's own opening.

techniques.name: Ferry Pole Primer (Sanh Độ Quyết)
techniques.concept: The ferry children's method, learned standing on a moving deck with a bamboo pole. The pole goes down into the river and Water qi comes up it; the bamboo itself gives a little Wood. At the sixth layer a ferryman can hold a loaded boat still against the spring current. Ashore it gives a steady body and good balance and not much more.

arts.concept: The holder vaults a short distance and the next blow she lands knocks the foe back.

techniques.lore: The boat families of the Nine-Bend River taught it to their children long before they banded together as a sect in 790 (A075).

techniques.name: Washing Waves Canon (Lãng Đào Kinh)
techniques.concept: Named for the gold-washers' saying that after a thousand washings the river sand gives up its gold (A076). The cultivator washes her own qi a thousand times through the meridians in a slow wave, and each layer leaves a little gold behind. In a fight the waves wash a foe's wards away one layer at a time, and what is left of the holder's qi at the end strikes clean through.

arts.concept: Each hit of the holder's Water arts strips a small part of the foe's ward; at the thousandth part (in practice, the tenth hit) the next art pierces fully.

techniques.lore: The founder Uông Liên Chu put it together from the boat families' songs and the gold-washers' rhythm after the feuds of 786-788 (V047, V048), so that the families would cultivate one method instead of feuding over landings.

techniques.name: Nine Bends Art (Cửu Khúc Quyết)
techniques.concept: The art of going round. A river does not break a rock; it bends nine times and arrives anyway. The holder slips each blow in a long curve, and every blow she slips builds a Bend; at nine Bends she arrives behind the foe with the whole river at her back. It is the sect's art for the elders and the head, and it is why Lãng Đào's ferries went round the serpent of the eighth bend for forty years instead of fighting it (A077).

arts.concept: After nine slipped blows, the holder's next Water art deals heavy damage from behind and cannot be evaded.

techniques.lore: Giang Cửu Khúc, whose name is the river's nine bends, holds it to the ninth layer. He says he has never once arrived late.
